newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Zedillo, in tax dispute, attacks corruption.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo, in tax dispute, attacks corruption.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo, who has launched a passionate defence of his own honesty during a dispute over alleged tax delinquency, on Thursday called for an end to all government corruption.
"We public servants have an obligation to be the first to observe the law," Zedillo told health workers.
"We will continue combating corruption among anyone who takes advantage of their posts to serve their particular interests, and who turn into accomplices of criminals," he told the health workers.
He was speaking the day after he launched an unusual defence of his reputation on national television, declaring: "I have been (honest) and will be all my life."

Zedillo has been accused by a leading opponent of being behind on some $1,000 in taxes owed for a property near the tourist resort of Acapulco, a rare allegation in a country where presidents are usually considered immune from legal attacks.

The president held a long interview with pro-government television anchorman Jacobo Zabludovsky late on Wednesday, denying any wrongdoing and saying he had been slandered, possibly for political reasons.

His accuser, Diego Fernandez de Cevallos, a fiery figure in the opposition National Action Party (PAN) and a former challenger to Zedillo in the 1994 presidential elections, on Thursday branded Zedillo "a liar."

Fernandez dented a long history of presidential "untouchability" in Mexico when he craftily aired his charge against Zedillo on national television, after calling up the station to first pay his respects to a dead bullfighter.
Zedillo has claimed success in his fight against corruption this year, arresting two generals on drug corruption charges.
But the arrests have cut both ways with the United States. Members of the U.S. Congress charged that they showed how high drug money reached in the Mexican government.
